[Anno domini M°CCCC°xix° in festo sanete trinitatis facta est conuencio census de incude Flaxlini (?) ad (sic) domino abbate Przibislao, ita quod idem Flaxlius debet dare ad festum Georii x gr. et in festo Galli totidem et non plus,] [Item in Chwaleticz Wenczeslaus et Jan babent de comunitate ibidem vnum hortum, de quo hortu soluunt annuatim de censu xn de. et pro eodem orto tenentur comunitatem non inpedire in pellendo eorum peccora ultra ipsorum agro«.] I5* 228 Anmerkungen. Vorstehendes Zinsbuch (liber censualis) ist durch sein Alter und seinen Inhalt eine gar nicht unbedeutende Quelle fиr die ältere Topographie des südlichen Böhmens. Si« ist namentlich nicht unbedeutend für Böhmen, wo derartige Quellen entweder noch nicht publicirt worden oder von dem Alter wie die vorliegende wahrscheinlich nur spärlich vorhanden sind. Nach Schrift und Inhalt ist dieses kleine Zinsbuch um das Jahr 1400 sehr sauber auf acht Pergamentblätter (in 8°, das erste Blatt ist unbeschrie ben) geschrieben worden. Die Zeilen stehen zwischen sorgfältig gezogenen Linien und es ist häufig zwischen ihnen ein Raum leer gelassen, um vielleicht spätere Eintragungen leichter vornehmen zu können. Die nicht innerhalb Klammern stehende Schrift ist die älteste. Was ich aber mit Klammern eingeschlossen habe, ist im Laufe des II>. Jahrhunderts von verschiedenen Händen eingetragen worden. Die Sternchen bedeuten, dass an dieser Stelle eine ganze Zeile ausradirt worden ist. Dieses älteste Zinsbuch des Stiftes Hohenfurt enthält ausser der Angabe der Zinse auch ein Verzeichniss der Jahrtage für die Gründer und Wohlthäter des Stiftes, das ich einmal schon wegen seines Alters und dann auch seiner Kürze wegen nicht weglassen mochte, und ein Verzeichniss der Pitanzien, d. h. der Speisen und des Weines, welche der Pitanzier (Küchen- und Kellermeister) an gewissen Tagen den Brüdern zu reichen hatte. Es hat letzteres Verzeichniss einigen culturhistorischen Werth, da sich aus ¡hm auf indirecte Weise abnehmen lässt, welch' einfache Lebensweise um 1400 bei den Brüdern Cisterciensern ¡n Hohenfurt herrschte. Das nächst älteste Zinsbuch des Stiftes ist im Jahre 1550 angelegt wor den. Es sei ferner hier bemerkt, dass, wenn es in den beigefügten Noten heisst: „Dieser Ort wird zuerst erwähnt" etc., dieses „zuerst" sich nur auf die Hohenfurter Urkunden bezieht. cxc. 1400. 30. April. Krumau. — Heinrich von Rosenberg verkauft dem Pfarrer Nikolaus von Höritz für die Höritzer Kirche 107 Groschen und einen Denar Zinse in dem Dorfe Straikowitz. Nos Henricus de Rosemberg recognoscimus vniuersis presenti- bus horum habituris noticiam, quia honorabilis vir dominus Nicolaus plebanus ecclesie in Horzicz dilectus nobis deo deuotus zelo sin cere caritatis accensus curaque bone voluntatis diem extremum judicii misericordie operibus diuine retribucionis intuitu cupiens preuenire, pro ecclesia sua ibidem in Horzicz, cuius tune rector 229 ipsemet cxistit et ad ruins perfeccionem totis viribus anhelauit, centum et septem grossos et vnum denarium pro vtroque termino, scilicet pro termino sancti Georgii quinquaginta et tres grossos et quatuor denarios et totidem pro termino sancti Galli, census annui perpetui in villa Strazkowicz in incolis subscriptis: in Ottone quindecim denarios, Henzlino Cues tredecim grossos minus vno (lunario, in Petro tredecim grossas minus vno denario, Henzlino Leucharthar tredecim grossos minus vno denario, in Hayndlino sex grossos cum tribus dcnariis et Pesskone Giskra sex grossos cum tribus denariis , vuamquamque sexagenam census eiusdem pro duo- decim sexagenis grossorum computando, certis ecclesie sue peccu- niis a nobis emit et legittime comparauit eidemque ecclesie sue census illos per se tune et deinde per successores suos omnes et singulos tenendos el colligendos perpetue jurisdicioni applicauit et incorporauit, nobi.sque omnia ilia ita nichilominus eidem ecclesie adaucta ft comparata cum singulis et vniuersis illis pertinenciis, que sic in- lo acquisitionis el comparaciouis titulo in presenti potuit uel in futuro poterit largicione Christi íidelium seu alio quouismodo adipisci, ad fideles manus nostras ad tabulas terre regni Boemie intabulauit, de nobis tamquam de patrono legittimu ac nostra de progenie seu successorum nostrorum posteritate gerens confidenciam singularem, nosque tarnen aut nostri posteri in bonis eisdem nullum jus obtinemus uel vnquam penitus obtinebunt. Sed tandummodo pro securitate dicti domini Nicolai ac suorum successorum seu ecclesie eiusdem pro securitate eandem acceptamus intabulationem. Sponde- mus igitur nos Henricus prenominatus fide pura et sincera presenti- hus sine dolo per nos beredes ac successores nostrns ratum firmum et gratum sic teneri et haberi fideliter, quatenus facientes iustum acceptum et dilectum deo et hominibus et predictis emptioni et applicaciuni et intabulacioni derogantes minime bona eadem predicta, ut prefertur, dicte eomparata et anexa ecclesie nullatenus impedia- mus molc.strimis uel pro nobis quomodolibet vsurpemus uel nostri successores vsurpent, ymmo efficaciter tueamur protegamus et defendamus bona ilia tamquam propria nostra. Sed quocumque anno, quocienscumque hoc eueneril, quod berna regia generaliter in toto regno «olíala fuerit, eandem nos Henricus predictus et successores tencbimur multum gratiosea buius census censualibus incolis accep- tare, inhibemus etiam vniuersis et singulis officialibus nostris speci 230 alitcrqiie tentoribus et rectoribus bonorum nostrnrum in Nouo Castro et in Crumpnaw precipue burgrawiis nostris ildelibus, qui eune suu't aut erunt pro tempore, districts et firmiter, ne predicte ecclesie homines et bona ipsius in hac nostre donacioni (sic) facta intabu- lacione impediant uel ab aliis permittant impediri, verum ipsa in ea manu quemadmodum et nos teneant protegant fauorabiliter defendant et conseruent, quoniam hec ipsa nostra et nostrum omnium sincera affectio tuicionis predictorum bonorum preamabilis suffragatrix nostrarum saluti enimarum efficietur, que nos vna cum emptore (?) census prenotati dilectissimo domino Nicolao plebano in Horzicz auctore domino deo abluet a peccatis et gratiam nobis restituet saluatoris. Vt autem hec prescripta nostra promissa robur expedite firmiter obtineant, presens scnptum fieri nostrique cum scitu pleno sigilli maioris ac cum sigillis famosorum virorum, puta Przibikonis de Zimunticz protunc purgrawii noslri in Crumpnaw et Woytyeuho- nis de Grasselow, qui cum bona sua voluntate nostrum ad affectum in testimonium sua sigilla appenderunt, nosque nostro sigillo pretuito presencia duximus munimine roborandum. Datum in Crum pnaw castro nosfro anno domini millesimo quadringentesimo feria sexta in vigilia sanctorum Philippi et Jacobi apostolorum. Das bereits beschriebene Siegel Heinrich's v. R. an einem Pergament- Streifen bangend ist allein mehr vorhanden.
entries.english:
CC. 1400. The oldest rent book of the monastery of Hohenfurt.

1400, 30 April, Krumau. Heinrich von Rosenberg sells to the priest Nikolaus of Höritz, for the church at Höritz, annual rents of 107 groschen and one denarius in the village of Straikowitz.

CLXXXIX. Folio II. The middle rent of Saint George belonging to the refectory, and likewise around the Feast of Saint Michael: at the manor of Lochowycz, ix shillings; at the bee yard, ix shillings. In the two clearings of Gerbert, xviii shillings and xx denarii; at Boldau and Bórsyglag, xiii shillings, xiiii denarii, and one obol. [And lx denarii from GMim awena, once a year.] At Lyebenthol, xiiii shillings less vi denarii. At Przyezowycz, Merawycz, Bona Aqua, and Kalycz, viii talents, iii shillings, and iii denarii; there, from the houses, xxviii denarii once a year. [And from a certain field, xx denarii once a year.] At Bt-stlens, lii denarii and one obol. At Ockol, x shillings. At the manor of Stokkem, [vi] shillings. [At Kyrigslog, i talent and vi denarii.] At Schestaw near Horzycz, iii shillings less v obols. [Also, from the mill near Stokharren, xiii groschen.] At Oppach and Czedlycz, xxi shillings and xl [ix denarii and one obol].

Editorial notes to these entries: The two “clearings” of Gerbert are the present-day villages of Unter-Schlagl and Gerbelschlag, both near the Austrian border. They came to the monastery as early as 1278. Boldau is now Waldau; the village is first mentioned in 1293, not yet as the monastery’s property but as belonging to a Rosenberg retainer. Bórsyglag is probably the village called Worsikslag in a 1343 charter, now perhaps Woisetschlag. Lyebenthol is now Uebenthal in the lower Mühlviertel; the monastery’s charters first mention it in 1378. Przyezowycz is now Pschieslowitz, or more correctly Prislowitz; the monastery acquired rents there in 1374. Merawycz is now Mörowitz; it is not possible to establish from charters when or how the monastery acquired the village. Bona Aqua is Gutwasser; the monastery acquired its rents in 1374. I think Kalycz should be read here; if so, it is the present village of Golitsch, first mentioned in a charter in 1341. I could not determine whether Bt-stlens still exists, or under what name. Ockol is now Oggold, which the monastery bought in 1349. The manor at Stokkem is now Stockernhof; the monastery received rents there as a gift in 1397. Kyrigslog is Kirchschlag, an old settlement first found in a charter of the monastery of Schlagl from 1283; the Hohenfurt rents there date from 1397. Schestaw is now Sehestau near Höritz; I first find it mentioned in Hohenfurt charters in 1372. The name Oppach has remained unchanged; the monastery acquired the village in 1281. Czedlycz is now Sedlitz near Krumau; it was given to the monastery as early as 1239.

Folio II continued. At Royken, Czwyenhlab (both villages), and Angrer, from one hide of vineyard, viii talents, iiii shillings, xi denarii. Of this, ix shillings are paid annually to the custodian for his refectory. At Seherleyns, vii talents, iii shillings, xii denarii. At Pukkaus, vii talents, x shillings, xxi denarii. Of this, x shillings and xii denarii are paid annually to the community. [Also there, for the weekly service on the Assumption, i sexagena and v groschen.] At Rosmberg, viii shillings from the steward. At Nusdorff, x shillings annually. At Horssaw, iii shillings less vi denarii. At Otyewyek, iii sexagena less viii denarii annually; of this, i talent is paid to the community. [And Wilhelm, steward of Rosenberg, pays xiii groschen.] [At Haczlow, xiii groschen and viii groschen from (?) Safran.] [Also at Kyssyelow, vi shillings; of this, lx denarii are paid annually to the custodian for flour for the altar breads.] [At Waykerstarff, iii shillings and i denarius once a year for the monks’ clothing.] [At Kyrigsslag, i talent is paid once a year to the custodian’s office for the altar breads at the early Mass.]

Notes: Royken is a name which I would identify with present-day Rukendorf or Roiden (?), but the form Rukchendorf, which I find in a 1278 charter, argues against the first identification. Czwyenhlab is now Zwinelag, which the monastery bought in 1344 according to the necrology of Jakob of Neuschloss. Angrer is now Angern, first mentioned in 1347; in a later charter the village has the Czech name Bugianow. Seherleyns is Sacheries, frequently found in the monastery’s charters; the monastery first acquired rents there in 1360. Pukkaus is now Buggaus; Wok von Rosenberg’s testament (1262) first names this place, but the monastery did not acquire it until 1377. Nusdorff is Nussdorf near Vienna, where the monastery already owned land in 1323. Horssaw is now Horischau; the monastery first acquired rents there in 1385. Otyewyek is also often written Oczyewyek; according to Palacký’s *Popis království českého*, it is Hochdorf. These rents date from 1387. Haczlow is now Hatzles, first mentioned in 1385. Kyssyelow is now Neustift in the parish of Schwarzbach (?) and is first mentioned in a charter in 1405. Waykerstarff is Weikersdorf in Upper Austria (Mühlviertel), where the Cistercians of Hohenfurt first appear as landowners in 1356.

Folio III. The middle rent of Saint George belonging to the community, and likewise around the Feast of Saint Michael. At Casclays and Wolech, vii talents [and xxxi denarii]. Of this, vi shillings less x denarii are given to the lord abbot, iii shillings to the custodian, and iiii denarii and one obol to the almoner. At Suchdol, [vi talents, xv denarii, one obol, xl groschen, and xii denarii]. Of this, [v shillings and vi denarii are given to the custodian, and vii shillings, xxii denarii, and one obol to the almoner]. At Walchunow, [xiii shillings, liii denarii, and one obol]. At Otyewyek, i talent. At Rayntol, x shillings and x denarii. At Bukowsk, v shillings and vi denarii. At Zabylays, ii sexagena and xxvi denarii. At Chwaletycz, ii sexagena less vi denarii. At Gebraslag, vii talents less xxx denarii. At Marthatislag, xxx denarii from a certain field. Also, from the mill at Slagel beneath Rosperg, xxi denarii. From all these revenues, once a year, xxx groschen are paid for the meal of the late Lord Peter von Rosenberg. On that same day, xl [units] are given to the poor at the gate.

The notes identify Casclays as perhaps “Hasclays” (Hatzles) or “Castlays,” in which case it might be present-day Kastlern; Wolech is present-day Wallachen. Neither place occurs in charters before 1500. Suchdol is now Suchenthal, where the monastery first acquired rents in 1366. Walchunow is first found in the same form in charters in 1405; if it is not identical with present-day Walketschlag (a place called Walkunslag is documented in 1363), it no longer exists, as far as I know. For Otyewyek, see note 25 above. The place-name Rayntol is not found in Bohemia; it should probably not be identified with Reichenthal in the Mühlviertel, where the monastery acquired property by purchase from Bernhard von Harach in 1387. For Zabylays and Bukowsk, see notes 21 and 22. Chwaletycz, first mentioned in the monastery’s charters in 1385, is Chwaletitz. Gebraslag is Gerbetschlag; see no. 3. Marthatislag is now Martetschlag, first documented in 1384. Slagel beneath Rosperg is the clearing at Rossberg. The monastery did not acquire this settlement until 1500; it seems, however, to be as old as the two clearings of Gerbert and, if I am not mistaken, is called the third clearing of Gerbert somewhere.

Folio III continued. [For light, the custodian receives one sexagena less xxx groschen.] The chamberlain receives xv talents for vessels. [For the lamp of Stephen, the custodian receives less xx denarii and i … (so in the source).] [For the lamp of the Holy Cross, i talent.] [For the lamp in the chapel of the Blessed Virgin and candles for “Salve Regina,” x shillings and xii denarii.] [For the lamp before the chapel of the sick, half a talent.] [For the tithe sold at Passerslog and Czypin, iii sexagena.] [At Gasllass there is also a special meadow, from which xvi denarii are paid each year, half at the Feast of Saint George and half at the Feast of Saint Gall; Simon Chromar holds that meadow.] [The total annual rent belonging to the community is altogether lxvi talents, vii shillings, and xxvi denarii. The person administering it must give xxx talents and lxii denarii to the assigned offices.]

Folio IV. [Total annual rent belonging to the almonry, from which the almoner must distribute certain portions to the assigned places and use the remainder to carry out the almonry’s work: altogether cxii talents less vi denarii.]

Folio V. Note: On the day after the Purification, the anniversary of Lady Johancze von Wellessyn is observed with one sexagena and twenty poor people. On the day after Saint Benedict’s day, the anniversary of Lord Dyethochon is observed with twenty-five poor people; a meal of one talent is given. On the Tuesday after Easter, the anniversary of Mykssykon of Hodonicz is observed, and the convent is given a meal of fifty groschen; of this, lxx denarii are given to the poor at the gate.

The notes identify Passauerschlag as now Passern, a place already recorded in 1291; Czypin is now Zippendorf, and the charters of the monastery often mention the name of a knightly family living there. Gasllass may again be Hatzles. For this and the following notices, compare the monastery’s necrology and the chronicle of Jakob of Neuschloss.

Folio V continued. On the third day after Saint Bartholomew’s Day, the anniversary of Lords Heinrich von Rosenberg and Hermann von Mylitz is observed with forty poor people; the convent is given a meal of one sexagena. On the day after Saint Peter ad Vincula, the anniversary of Nicolaus called Przyporzycze, purgrave of Wildstein, is observed, and the convent is given a meal of one talent. On the third day after Saint Nicholas’s Day, the anniversary of Lord Heinrich von Plumau is observed with forty poor people; a meal of one sexagena is given. The anniversary of Lady Ofcze is observed after Easter; a meal of one talent is given. On Saint Dionysius’s Day, the anniversary of Lord Gregorius of Herslag is observed; the convent is given a meal of ix shillings.

Folio VI. The anniversary of Steynprechar is observed during Advent; a meal of one talent is given. The anniversary of Woytyechon of Gywowycz is observed; a meal of one talent less viii denarii is given. [The anniversary of Weczlin of Cypyn is observed on Saint Nicholas’s Day, or on the day of his death; the convent is given a meal of one sexagena of groschen and xii denarii. The poor receive xlii denarii from this.] [The anniversary of Lord Peter, priest of Rosis, is also observed; on that day the convent is given viii shillings and the poor xl groschen—and on Saint Edmund’s Day (?)]

Folio VII. Note what is given by way of the abbot’s refectory for the convent. On the vigil of the Nativity of Christ, two fish dishes, baked food, and [illegible] bread for one Heller, and wine are given. On the “holy day,” that is, Christmas Day, strawin and chach with one fish dish and wine are given. On the Circumcision, eggs in broth are given. On the Epiphany of the Lord, preding, niues, and chnechel are given, with wine and bread; if it falls on a vigil, wine is given as an extra. On Saint Benedict’s Day, figs, baked food, and wine are given once. On the Annunciation of the Lord, esoces, raisins, almonds, and baked food are given, with wine twice. On Palm Sunday, esones, figs, fish, baked food, and wine are given. On Maundy Thursday, double portions of esoces, fish, raisins, figs, wine, and baked food are given. On Easter Eve, double portions of esoces, raisins, figs, wine, and baked food are given. On Easter Day, two egg dishes and wine are given. On Ascension Day, two egg dishes, one fish dish, and wine are given. At Pentecost, two customary dishes, one fish dish, and wine are given.

Folio VIII. On the dedication of the church, two customary egg dishes and three fish dishes are given. On Corpus Christi, two customary egg dishes and wine are given. On the vigil of the Assumption of the Blessed Mary, two fish dishes, baked food, and wine are given. On the Feast of the Assumption of Saint Mary, two customary pittance dishes, one fish dish, and wine are given. On the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin, two customary pittance dishes, one fish dish, and wine are given. On All Saints’ Day, two pittance dishes and wine are given. [In the year of the Lord 1419, on the Feast of the Holy Trinity, an agreement was made with the abbot Przibislaus concerning the rent from Flaxlin’s anvil (?): Flaxlius must pay x groschen at the Feast of Saint George and the same at the Feast of Saint Gall, and no more.] [At Chwaletycz, Wenceslaus and Jan have a garden from the community; they pay an annual rent of xii denarii for it and are obliged not to hinder the community from driving its livestock beyond their fields.]

Editorial description of the rent book: The foregoing rent book (liber censualis), because of its age and contents, is a significant source for the early topography of southern Bohemia. It is particularly important for Bohemia, where sources of this kind have either not yet been published or are probably scarce at such an early date as this. Judging from its handwriting and contents, this small rent book was written very neatly around the year 1400 on eight parchment leaves in octavo; the first leaf is blank. The lines are between carefully ruled lines, and space is often left between them, perhaps to make later additions easier. The writing not enclosed in brackets is the oldest. What I have enclosed in brackets was added during the fifteenth century by different hands. The asterisks indicate places where an entire line has been erased. In addition to listing rents, this oldest rent book of Hohenfurt contains a list of anniversaries for the founders and benefactors of the monastery, which I did not want to omit both because of its age and its brevity. It also contains a list of pittances—that is, food and wine which the pittance master (the kitchen and cellar master) was to provide to the brothers on certain days. The latter list has some cultural-historical value, since it indirectly shows how simple the Cistercian brothers’ way of life at Hohenfurt was around 1400. The monastery’s next oldest rent book was drawn up in 1550. Finally, when the attached notes say that a place “is first mentioned,” this means only that it is first mentioned in the Hohenfurt charters.

CXC. 1400, 30 April, Krumau. Heinrich von Rosenberg sells to the priest Nikolaus of Höritz, for the church at Höritz, rents of 107 groschen and one denarius in the village of Straikowitz.

We, Heinrich von Rosenberg, make known to all who now or hereafter learn of this that the honorable man Lord Nikolaus, priest of the church at Höritz, dear to us and devoted to God, moved by the zeal of sincere charity and wishing through works of mercy to anticipate the final day of judgment in hope of divine reward, bought with funds belonging to his church one hundred and seven groschen and one denarius of perpetual annual rent for his church at Höritz, of which he is now the rector and whose repair he earnestly desires.

The rent is payable in two terms: at the Feast of Saint George, fifty-three groschen and four denarii, and the same amount at the Feast of Saint Gall. It is owed by the following inhabitants of the village of Straikowitz: Otto, fifteen denarii; Henzlin Cues, thirteen groschen less one denarius; Peter, thirteen groschen less one denarius; Henzlin Leucharthar, thirteen groschen less one denarius; Hayndlin, six groschen and three denarii; and Pessko Giskra, six groschen and three denarii. Each sexagena of this rent is reckoned as twelve sexagena of groschen.

He lawfully bought this rent for the church and incorporated it into the church’s perpetual jurisdiction, to be held and collected by him and thereafter by each of his successors. He also entered all these properties, thus increased and acquired for the church, together with all appurtenances which it has acquired by purchase and may acquire in future through the generosity of Christ’s faithful or by any other means, in the land tables of the Kingdom of Bohemia, placing them in our faithful hands. He showed singular confidence in us as his lawful patron and in our descendants and successors; nevertheless, neither we nor our descendants have or shall ever have any right in these properties. We accept this registration solely for the security of Lord Nikolaus, his successors, and his church.

Therefore, I, the aforesaid Heinrich, promise in pure and sincere good faith, without deceit, for myself, my heirs, and successors, to uphold and honor this arrangement faithfully. We shall not hinder or trouble the aforesaid church’s properties, duly acquired and attached to it as stated above; neither shall we or our successors in any way usurp them. Rather, we shall protect and defend these properties as our own. Whenever the royal tax is levied generally throughout the kingdom, I, the aforesaid Heinrich, and my successors shall require the tenants paying this rent to contribute a very moderate share toward that tax.

We strictly forbid all our officials, especially the keepers and administrators of our properties at Nové Hrady and Krumau, and above all our loyal burgraves, present and future, to hinder or permit others to hinder the people and properties of the aforesaid church in connection with this registration of our grant. Instead, they shall hold, protect, favorably defend, and preserve them as we do. For our sincere concern for the protection of these properties will aid the salvation of our souls, and, together with the purchaser of the aforesaid rent, our dear Lord Nikolaus, priest of Höritz, will, by the grace of God, cleanse us of our sins and restore the Savior’s favor to us.

To ensure that these promises remain fully and firmly in force, we have had this document written and secured with our great seal, together with the seals of two distinguished men: Przibiko von Zimuntitz, then our purgrave at Krumau, and Woytyechon von Grasselow, who willingly attached their seals in witness to our purpose. We have also strengthened these presents with our own seal. Given at our castle of Krumau in the year of the Lord 1400, on Friday, the vigil of Saints Philip and James the Apostles. Only the already described seal of Heinrich von Rosenberg, hanging from a parchment strip, remains.
